flags.headline: Hormuz conflict escalated over the weekend — fresh US-Iran airstrikes, oil +6-7% on the week, not yet priced into the book
flags.detail: Escalation, not de-escalation, since Friday: fresh U.S. and Iranian airstrikes over the weekend renewed the fighting that had already brought Strait of Hormuz shipping to a near-standstill (only ~34 ships/day transiting vs. the normal ~88). Brent crude futures jumped 7% on the week to above $77-79/bbl; WTI climbed 6% to above $72. U.S. equity futures are wavering pre-open (Nasdaq -0.89%, S&P -0.23%, Dow +0.13% as of ~5:38am ET) on the tension plus CPI (Tue) and the start of bank earnings (Tue: C, GS, WFC, JPM, BAC). Today's Risk Data Drop still reflects Friday's close for every name, so none of this is in the book's current prices — it is a before-the-open heads-up, not a confirmed move. Direction for the energy sleeve is genuinely two-sided: DVN and CVX (upstream) generally benefit from higher oil prices, while VLO (refiner) faces crack-spread and input-cost uncertainty, and CNX (natural gas, not directly Hormuz-linked) is largely a bystander. Escalated to RED for the surprise/gap-risk factor and the volume of stacked catalysts this week, not because any specific held name's thesis has broken.

flags.headline: AEM — persisting RED, Barnat production-cut risk unresolved, formal update still due 7/29
flags.detail: No new development this run.
